decisions.question: How should this work be decomposed into slices? The work spans: (A) `submit_task` epic-input handling + issue-type detection, (B) refine prompt tweaks + apply step (`editJiraIssue` on epic Description), (C) plan prompt tweaks for per-node ticket-shaped descriptions, (D) plan apply step (`createJiraIssue` + `createIssueLink` + plan-node→key mapping), (E) orchestrator-direct Jira creds + Won't-Do transitions for reassess, (F) reassess-specific planning (consolidate/split/diff), (G) in-flight child detection (status + open-PR cross-check + remote-link fallback) + per-ticket HITL gating.

options.label: Single slice: all parts ship together — [A+B+C+D+E+F+G] (1 PR)
Two slices with dependency: [foundation: A+B+C+D+E fresh-epic only] -> [reassess: F+G] (2 PRs)
Three slices with dependency: [foundation: A+B+C fresh refine] -> [planner+apply: D+E fresh] -> [reassess+in-flight: F+G] (3 PRs)
Two slices in parallel: [fresh-epic path: A+B+C+D+E] || [reassess+in-flight infra: F+G+E-reassess] (2 PRs, but B/D shared scope will need careful merge)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: **Hierarchy mechanism for child Jira tickets**: which field links children to the epic? Jira projects vary — older "Classic" company-managed projects use the `Epic Link` custom field, newer "Next-gen" / team-managed projects use the native `parent` field, and some projects support both. The gateway's `create_issue` accepts both `parent` and `epic_link` (mutually exclusive). How should the plan apply step decide which one to set?

options.label: Auto-detect from the target epic's project: probe Jira project metadata once at submit_task time and cache the choice for the rest of the pipeline
Always prefer `parent`; fall back to `Epic Link` only if `parent` create fails
Operator-configurable per Jira project (config file mapping project key -> field choice); error if no mapping found and ambiguous
Operator-supplied as a `submit_task` parameter (e.g. `jira_hierarchy_field`); default to `parent`
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: **Reassess Won't Do transitions — batch vs per-ticket HITL**: when the reassess plan flags some pre-existing children as obsolete, should the orchestrator transition them all to Won't Do on plan approval, or require a separate per-ticket HITL confirmation? In-flight children (status mid-workflow OR has an open PR) already have a per-ticket HITL gate per the issue's resolved sub-section, so this question is about *Done≠relevant* and *To Do→Won't Do* transitions on non-in-flight children only.

options.label: Single plan approval applies all Won't Do transitions atomically (operator sees the obsolete list in the plan draft and approves wholesale)
Per-ticket HITL gate for every Won't Do transition (each obsolete ticket gets its own decision in the HITL surface, mirroring the in-flight gate)
Single approval for *To Do* obsolete children; per-ticket gate only when transitioning a child that has any non-trivial history (comments, prior transitions, or linked tickets)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: **Done children handling in the plan prompt**: when reassessing an epic that has children already in Done state, how should those Done children be presented to the planning agent?

options.label: Exclude Done children from the plan prompt entirely (cleanest signal — agent can't accidentally re-propose equivalent work)
Include Done children with an explicit `do-not-re-plan` marker (gives the agent context for what's already shipped so it can build on it; risk is the agent might re-propose anyway)
Include Done children's summary+description but redact acceptance criteria + scope (gives just enough context for follow-on planning without inviting re-implementation)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: **Consolidation survivor selection (N existing children → 1 plan node)**: when the reassess plan consolidates multiple existing tickets into a single node, which existing key should survive (edited in place) and which should be transitioned to Won't Do with a redirect comment?

options.label: Oldest ticket survives (lowest issue number) — preserves the longest history and link-graph
Most-linked ticket survives (most inward/outward issue links + comments + watchers) — minimizes link-graph rewiring
Agent picks per-consolidation with rationale in the plan draft; operator can override per-node before approval
First N-of-N retained by creation order (no heuristic, deterministic only)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: **Implement-phase trigger for created children**: after a plan is approved and child tickets are created in Jira, how should the implement phase get kicked off?

options.label: Manual: operator runs `submit_task <CHILD-KEY>` for each new child when ready (today's behavior for any Jira ticket; epic apply step just creates the tickets and stops)
Auto-spawn: orchestrator automatically calls `submit_task <CHILD-KEY>` for every created child immediately after plan approval (parallel kickoff of every leaf in the cross-task DAG)
Auto-spawn topologically: orchestrator spawns root nodes of the cross-task DAG immediately; downstream nodes spawn as their dependencies complete (respects `Blocks` / `Is blocked by` edges)
Auto-spawn opt-in: a `submit_task` parameter (e.g. `auto_implement_children=true`) controls whether the epic pipeline cascades into children
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: **Confluence link discovery scope** during refine: where should the agent look for Confluence pages to pull?

options.label: Jira `remoteLinks` only (issue/{key}/remotelink); structured + reliable
Remote links + URL-scrape the epic description and existing-children descriptions for Confluence page URLs
Remote links + description URLs + linked Jira issues' remote links (recursive one level)
Operator-supplied list only (no auto-discovery) — pass Confluence page IDs as a `submit_task` parameter
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: **In-flight detection signal precedence**: the issue lists three signals — Jira `fields.status.name` mid-workflow, orchestrator pipeline state with an open PR artifact, and Jira `remoteLinks` parsing for `github.com/.../pull/`. When two signals disagree (e.g. Jira status says `To Do` but orchestrator has an open PR), which wins for the `in_flight` classification?

options.label: OR semantics (any positive signal => in_flight): conservative, may over-gate but never under-gates
Orchestrator pipeline state wins (truth source: we know we shipped a PR); Jira status is informational only
Jira status wins (truth source: workflow state); orchestrator PR is informational only
OR for `in_flight`-flag, but the *signal source* is logged on the HITL gate so the operator sees which signal fired
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: **Reassess refine-output strategy**: when reassessing an epic that already has a Description on the Jira ticket, what should the refine apply step do with it?

options.label: Wholesale rewrite: replace the existing Description with the refined analysis (clean, but loses any operator-curated content)
Refined analysis appended/merged below a `## Previous Description` heading; agent prompt instructs to integrate and supersede where possible
Append-only: existing Description retained as-is; refined analysis added below an `## Updated Analysis (<date>)` heading (safest, but Description grows unboundedly across re-runs)
Operator chooses per-run via HITL at refine-approval time (offer rewrite vs merge as a separate decision in the analysis draft)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: **Plan-node → Jira-key mapping persistence**: the issue says "Plan draft records the mapping from plan nodes → Jira keys so re-runs are idempotent." Where should this mapping live so subsequent re-runs (e.g. a second reassess) can find it?

options.label: Inline yaml-frontmatter block at the top of `.egg-state/drafts/<id>-plan.md` (human-readable + version-controlled in the work branch)
Separate `.egg-state/drafts/<id>-plan-mapping.yaml` file alongside the plan draft (cleaner separation; same branch)
Persisted as a pipeline artifact in `.egg-state/pipelines/<id>.json` under a new `epic_apply` key (matches today's `pr_url` artifact pattern; survives draft rewrites)
Stored on the epic's Jira ticket via a hidden custom field or a tagged Description footer (survives independent of the egg repo — strongest cross-environment idempotency)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: **Apply-step execution location**: regardless of how the work is sliced (decision-1), the plan-phase needs to know where the apply step's gateway calls (`editJiraIssue`, `createJiraIssue`, `createIssueLink`, `addCommentToJiraIssue`) actually originate. This is a trust-boundary choice orthogonal to slicing. The Won't-Do transition is unambiguously orchestrator-only (no gateway path); the rest can go either way.

options.label: In-sandbox-agent for all gateway-mediated writes (a dedicated `apply-epic` agent runs after refine/plan approval and calls the gateway). Won't-Do transitions still orchestrator-only. Preserves gateway audit identity = session token; one extra agent invocation per phase.

Orchestrator-side for all writes (orchestrator opens its own gateway session token and issues the create/edit/link calls directly). Avoids the extra agent; introduces a new orchestrator-side gateway client + audit-identity story for non-transition writes.

Hybrid: gateway-mediated writes from a dedicated `apply-epic` agent for everything except `transitions`; orchestrator-only for `transitions` (the gateway-blocked verb). Maximises symmetry with today's 'agents write through the gateway' pattern.

All-orchestrator with no agent in the data path (writes go directly to Jira from the orchestrator using its credential surface, bypassing the gateway for create/edit/link as well). Worst symmetry, biggest cred surface; only worth considering if the gateway's create/edit/link become a bottleneck.
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: **Reassess-trigger override on `submit_task`** (promoted from feedback-1 Q5 in response to NACK — structurally a decision, not open-ended feedback): `submit_task <EPIC-KEY>` auto-detects the reassess path when the epic has children. Should the operator be able to force the path explicitly?

options.label: No override: auto-detection only (smallest surface; operator must transition children away from the epic if they want a fresh-path treatment)

Add `--reassess` / `--fresh` mutex flags on `submit_task` to force the path. `--fresh` on an epic with children warns + asks the operator to confirm; `--reassess` on an epic with no children no-ops gracefully into the fresh path.
Single `--mode={auto,reassess,fresh}` parameter on `submit_task`; default `auto` preserves today's behavior, explicit overrides bypass detection without confirmation.
Add a non-`submit_task` `egg <whatever> reassess <EPIC-KEY>` admin subcommand for forced reassess, leaving `submit_task` auto-detect-only (keeps `submit_task` surface clean).
Other (explain in reply)

How should these credentials be provisioned and protected? Options to consider: env vars (e.g. `EGG_ORCH_JIRA_EMAIL`/`EGG_ORCH_JIRA_TOKEN`); a config file path; the existing gateway credential store (with a separate scope tag); a per-project credential map. Whichever path is chosen, please also clarify: (a) the operator-facing setup story (where they put the creds, how rotation works); (b) audit/logging expectations for transitions performed by the orchestrator.

Should we mandate a fixed structure in the plan prompt (e.g. `Problem statement / Scope / Acceptance criteria / Out of scope / Cross-links`) or leave the shape to the agent's judgement per node? Are there other link types operator-side projects use that we should support (e.g. `Relates to`, `Causes`)? Should the plan prompt allow the agent to choose the link type per edge, or always emit `Blocks` for cross-task DAG edges?
